3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 10

Writing about myself

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Write a short text about yourself: name, age, family, likes and abilities
  • Use capital letters, full stops and the connectors and, but, because
  • Plan a text with a mind map before writing
  • Check and improve your writing with a checklist

Para pensar

Tienes un amigo por correspondencia en Inglaterra y quieres presentarte por escrito. ¿Qué cosas le contarías de ti y cómo lo ordenarías?

Explicación

All about me

Writing about yourself is a great way to use all the English you know. In a text about you, you can write: your name and age, where you live, what you look like, your family and pets, what you like and what you can do.

You already know the sentences! «I'm Carla.» «I'm eight.» «I've got a brother.» «I like pizza.» «I can swim.» Ahora solo hay que ordenarlas y unirlas para que formen un texto bonito.

Plan first: a mind map

Before writing, make a mind map (mapa de ideas). Write ME in the centre. Draw lines to five bubbles: name and age, home, family, likes and abilities. In each bubble, write words, not sentences: «Carla, 8», «Sevilla, flat», «1 brother, 1 cat», «pizza, dancing», «swim, draw».

The mind map helps you remember everything and put it in order. Consejo: los buenos escritores siempre planifican antes de escribir, ¡hasta en su lengua materna!

Sentences that start with I

Most sentences in your text start with I. Ojo: en inglés, I (yo) se escribe siempre con mayúscula, aunque esté en mitad de la frase: «My sister and I like music.»

Use the key verbs: I'm + name, age or adjective («I'm friendly»), I live in + place, I've got + family, pets, hair and eyes, I like / I love + things, I can + abilities. With these five you can write a lot!

Capital letters and full stops

Every sentence starts with a capital letter (mayúscula) and ends with a full stop (punto). «My name is Carla.» We also use capital letters for: names (Carla, Leo), places (Sevilla, Spain), days and months (Monday, May), languages and nationalities (English, Spanish) and I.

En castellano: en español «lunes», «mayo» y «español» van en minúscula. En inglés, no: Monday, May, Spanish llevan mayúscula.

Joining ideas: and, but, because

Short sentences are OK, but we can join them with connectors to make the text better. And (y) adds ideas: «I like dogs and cats.» But (pero) shows a contrast: «I can swim, but I can't dive.» Because (porque) gives a reason: «I love Saturdays because I play football.»

Compare: «I've got a cat. I've got a dog.» → «I've got a cat and a dog.» ¡Queda mucho mejor! Intenta usar cada conector al menos una vez.

Paragraphs

A good text has got paragraphs (párrafos): groups of sentences about the same idea. For a text about you, you can write three paragraphs. Paragraph 1: name, age, home and appearance. Paragraph 2: family and pets. Paragraph 3: likes, hobbies and abilities.

Start with a greeting, «Hello!» or «Hi!», and finish with a goodbye: «Write soon!» or «Bye for now!». Each paragraph starts on a new line.

A model text

Read Carla's text: «Hello! My name's Carla and I'm eight years old. I live in a flat in Sevilla, in Spain. I've got long black hair and brown eyes.

I've got one brother, Leo, and a cat called Misi. My grandma lives with us. I love reading comics and dancing. My favourite food is pizza. I can swim very well, but I can't ride a horse. I love Saturdays because I go to the beach with my family. Write soon! Carla»

Check your writing

When you finish, read your text again and use a checklist: ✓ Have I got a greeting and a goodbye? ✓ Does every sentence start with a capital letter and end with a full stop? ✓ Is I always a capital letter? ✓ Have I used and, but and because? ✓ Have I written about my family, likes and abilities?

You can also swap texts with a partner and give two stars and a wish: two things you like and one thing to improve. «I like your connectors. I like your pet. Wish: use more capital letters.»

Let's practise: my «All about me» poster

Now it's your turn! 1) Make your mind map. 2) Write your text in three paragraphs. 3) Check it with the checklist. 4) Copy it neatly onto a big card, with a photo or a self-portrait in the middle.

Hang the posters on the wall and do a gallery walk: walk around, read your classmates' posters and find something in common: «Lucas likes dogs too!», «Ana can swim, like me!». ¿Cuántas cosas en común encuentras?

Writing about myself

Ejercicios

  1. Escribe una frase con tu nombre y tu edad.

  2. Escribe dónde vives.

  3. Describe tu pelo y tus ojos.

  4. Pon mayúsculas: «on monday i speak english».

  5. Une con but: «I can draw. I can't sing.»

  6. Completa con because: «I like Fridays ___ I go swimming.»

  7. ¿Qué es un mind map?

  8. Escribe un saludo y una despedida para tu texto.

  9. Escribe dos cosas que comprobar al terminar.

  10. Escribe un párrafo de 4 frases sobre ti.

Practica

  1. Before writing, we make a…

    1. A) full stop
    2. B) mind map
    3. C) poster

  2. The word I is always…

    1. A) a capital letter
    2. B) a small letter
    3. C) in red

  3. A sentence ends with a…

    1. A) capital letter
    2. B) comma
    3. C) full stop

  4. Which needs a capital letter?

    1. A) dog
    2. B) pizza
    3. C) Monday

  5. I like cats ___ dogs.

    1. A) and
    2. B) but
    3. C) because

  6. I can swim, ___ I can't dive.

    1. A) and
    2. B) but
    3. C) because

  7. I love Sundays ___ I visit my grandma.

    1. A) because
    2. B) but
    3. C) and

  8. «I've got a brother» talks about…

    1. A) abilities
    2. B) likes
    3. C) family

  9. «I can ride a bike» talks about…

    1. A) family
    2. B) abilities
    3. C) home

  10. A good goodbye is…

    1. A) Hello!
    2. B) Write soon!
    3. C) I'm eight.

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué cosas puedo contar en un texto sobre mí; Cómo planifico con un mapa de ideas; Qué palabras llevan mayúscula en inglés; Cómo uno ideas con and, but y because y reviso mi texto.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

mind mapMapa de ideas para planificar.
capital letterMayúscula: I, Monday, Spain.
full stopPunto al final de la frase.
andY: añade ideas.
butPero: contraste.
becausePorque: da una razón.
paragraphGrupo de frases sobre una idea.
checklistLista para revisar el texto.

Soluciones

  1. B) Plan.
  2. A) Mayúscula.
  3. C) Punto.
  4. C) Días con mayúscula.
  5. A) Añadir: and.
  6. B) Contraste: but.
  7. A) Razón: because.
  8. C) Familia.
  9. B) Habilidad.
  10. B) Despedida.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. My name's… and I'm… years old.
  2. I live in… (ciudad o pueblo).
  3. I've got short brown hair and green eyes (por ejemplo).
  4. On Monday I speak English.
  5. I can draw, but I can't sing.
  6. because.
  7. Un mapa de ideas para planificar antes de escribir.
  8. Hello! … Write soon! (o Bye for now!).
  9. Mayúsculas y puntos; usar and, but y because.
  10. Model answer: Hello! I'm Mario and I'm nine. I live in Zaragoza. I've got a sister and I love football because it's fun.
